correctness.rationale: For every residue r, the known Apéry formula w(r)=F_a beta(r)+r proves membership iff the quotient is >= beta(r). Zeckendorf uniqueness yields B_a=B_(a-1)||(1+B_(a-2)). At positive row levels the appended initial digit equals one, preventing run crossing; the only extra run in that piece at level one has length F_(a-2)-1. This proves exact multiset recurrence R_a=R_(a-1) ⊎ R_(a-2) ⊎ {F_(a-2)-1} with empty R_3,R_4 and solves it uniformly for all a>=5. Direct independent finite DP and Zeckendorf calculations for a=5..24 agree with all 46,365 blocks; finite verification does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The full shifted-Fibonacci semigroup Apéry theorem is known (Robles-Pérez--Rosales, 2022). A published same-family isolated-gap result already covers the length-one count, and the available pseudo-Frobenius and broader r-Fibonacci results address distinct invariants. This claim instead evaluates every maximal gap-block length and its multiplicity by proving a new run-multiset Fibonacci recurrence. Full primary materials and actual semantic matching were compared. Implicit specialization in unindexed work remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: A theorem on run distributions in Fibonacci words or on Apéry threshold words may give this law in equivalent notation despite no matching search result.
A general semigroup result could make the Fibonacci specialization immediate upon nontrivial substitution; no exhaustive global bibliography exists.
The exact length-one case is already published and is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim as an independent finding.

value.rationale: Maximal consecutive omitted-integer lengths are intrinsic semigroup gap invariants, refining genus, Frobenius number, and the known isolated-gap census. The theorem supplies the entire natural length histogram at arbitrarily many Fibonacci scales and an exact structural recursion, including the absent penultimate Fibonacci scale and exact number of blocks. It is not a numerical table or a simple substitution into an already proved run-frequency result.
